I'm just now getting into bitcoin and I just installed BTCCore on my Linux machine.

As soon as I started it, it began to download what seems like the history of all transactions ever made with bitcoin in /home/user/.bitcoin/blocks.
It got to about 7GB and there are still 2 years left!

Is this process mandatory? do I have to keep the data? if not so, How to delete it? what part of it (not) to delete?

Sorry for the many questions, have a nice day (night) :]
Bitcoin Core is downloading massive pack of data (!)

Bitcoin Core has the entire blockchain in it, which is 30+GB atm. Which is needed to verify transactions.

If you don't want that many data, you can try a light client like electrum.
Thank you. I'm also a beginner and was wondering about this.
You could also run Bitcoin Core 0.11 release candidate with pruning enabled, if you're feeling adventurous.
He's been using it as his wallet, which I believe isn't an option with pruning enabled as historic blocks cannot be served.

Yeah, that is necessary if you want to run the core client. As mentioned, you can use a lightweight client like electrum, or if you are really lazy (and not that concerned about keeping your money safe) you can use a web wallet.

Thank you all very much, I switched to Electrum and I'll stick to it, it seems good and fast enough.

Also more complete that btccore.

Yes, "what seems like the history of all transactions ever made with bitcoin" that was downloading to your computer was indeed the entire transaction history - called the blockchain.

If you are willing and have what you need, you should run a full node (i.e. Bitcoin Core) to support the network, but you don't have to.

From your comments I see that you've started useing Electrum. That's great, but you should make sure that you realize the privacy risks behind using this wallet. Any wallet that doesn't have a full copy of the blockchain will have some of the privacy risks that Electrum has, but you should be careful anyway.

P.S. - Make sure you save a good backup of your wallet! (the seed, if you use Electrum) This is critical to recover your bitcoin if anything goes wrong with your hard drive. And welcome to bitcoin!
